spec.description: Public-view health of Graph Protocol components, exported by graph-monitor. Nothing here is graded by the tool: it reports what it read, and this dashboard (and its alert rules) decide what is acceptable.

spec.title: Accounts now
spec.description: One row per account. Blank cells mean that check is not configured for that account — not that it is zero.

spec.expr: max by (network, group, account, address) (gm_account_eth_balance{network=~"$network", group=~"$group", account=~"$account"})
max by (network, group, account, address) (gm_account_grt_balance{network=~"$network", group=~"$group", account=~"$account"})
max by (network, group, account, address) (gm_account_idle_seconds{network=~"$network", group=~"$group", account=~"$account"})
max by (network, group, account, address) (gm_account_activity_seen{network=~"$network", group=~"$group", account=~"$account"})

spec.title: ETH balance
spec.description: Solid lines are balances. A dashed line is that account's configured top-up trigger, shown only where remediation is configured.

spec.title: Time since last activity
spec.description: Time since the account last did the thing it exists to do, measured at the pinned block. A line climbing without resetting is an account that has gone quiet. Log scale, so an account quiet for months does not flatten the ones measured in hours. With a subgraph source, quiet accounts keep a value past their lookback instead of turning unreadable.

spec.title: Not seen in the lookback
spec.description: Read successfully, nothing within the account's lookback. Empty is the healthy state, and this is NOT the same as an unreadable check. Quiet for = time since the last event, when known (a subgraph source knows it past the lookback); blank means no event was ever found.

spec.expr: max by (network, group, account) (gm_account_activity_seen{network=~"$network", group=~"$group", account=~"$account"}) == 0

max by (network, group, account) (gm_account_idle_seconds{network=~"$network", group=~"$group", account=~"$account"}) and on (network, group, account) (max by (network, group, account) (gm_account_activity_seen{network=~"$network", group=~"$group", account=~"$account"}) == 0)

spec.title: GRT allowances
spec.description: Use the Unlimited column, not Raw GRT: an unlimited approval is ~1.157e59 and a float cannot represent it faithfully. That column is computed on exact integers.

spec.expr: max by (network, group, owner, spender) (gm_allowance_unlimited{network=~"$network", group=~"$group"})
max by (network, group, owner, spender) (gm_allowance_exact_max{network=~"$network", group=~"$group"})
max by (network, group, owner, spender) (gm_allowance_grt{network=~"$network", group=~"$group"})

spec.title: Source
spec.description: Up only if every source passed verification: each network's RPC and any subgraph source. Which one is down: see Sources now.

spec.title: Subgraphs now
spec.description: One row per subgraph check: the published version, plus each listed deployment. Up means it answered, from the expected deployment, without indexing errors and within max_lag. "Not checked" means our side failed (e.g. API key) and says nothing about the subgraph. Blank cells mean that number could not be measured this cycle, not that it is zero. Subgraphs on every chain are listed, not just the selected network; Blocks behind is only measured for the chain graph-monitor's RPC serves. Not checked = gm_subgraph_readable is 0. Fault = why it is down or not checked: unreachable, stale, wrong_deployment, indexing_errors (down); not_configured, key_rejected (not checked, our side).

spec.title: Subgraph lag
spec.description: How far each subgraph's latest indexed block trails the wall clock. A line that stops means the subgraph could not be read.

spec.title: Check failures
spec.description: Rising here while the source stays up usually means a provider limit — block range or rate — rather than an outage.

spec.title: Cycle duration
spec.description: If p95 approaches the serve interval, cycles start skipping ticks.

spec.title: Check duration p95
spec.description: Activity checks dominate: they scan logs backwards and cost scales with how far back they must look. Subgraph and network checks are one query each.

spec.title: Remediation outcomes
spec.description: Empty unless --remediate is on. `failed` is the one to alert on: an auto-fix that is broken is more urgent than the balance that triggered it.

spec.title: Cycle age
spec.description: Seconds since a cycle last read anything. This is the deadman: `up` catches a dead process, this catches one that is alive but wedged.

spec.title: Unreadable
spec.description: Checks that could not read, of every kind: account, allowance, subgraph and network checks. NOT the same as a bad value: the tool is blind there, usually a provider limit, an outage or a missing API key. The fault kind is in gm_<subject>_fault{kind}.

spec.title: Source lag
spec.description: The worst lag across all sources. Per source: see Sources now.

spec.title: Block
spec.description: Every value on this dashboard was read at these heights, one per network.

spec.title: Version
spec.description: Running build, for lining a change in behaviour up against a deploy.

spec.title: Sources now
spec.description: What graph-monitor reads from: each network's RPC (rpc:<network>) and any subgraph source (subgraph:<label>). Verified every cycle before anything is read through it. Down means the tool is blind to what it serves: every watch on a down RPC's network is unreadable; a down subgraph source makes activity watches fall back to searching the chain. Fault = why a source is down: unreachable, stale, chain_id_mismatch, state_unavailable, wrong_deployment, indexing_errors, not_configured or key_rejected.

spec.title: Solo deployments by indexer
spec.description: Per indexer: deployments it is the only one allocated to, that have curation signal and are not denied rewards, and the GRT signalled on them. Read from the network-monitoring subgraph by the solo_deployments network check ([checks.<network>] solo_deployments = true). No indexer is excluded: the upgrade indexer (0xbdfb5ee5a2abf4fc7bb1bd1221067aef7f9de491) is expected to have many. Empty with gm_network_readable{check="solo_deployments"} = 0 means the check could not read, not that there are none.

spec.title: Solo deployments, top indexers
spec.description: The ten indexers with the most solo deployments over time. A step up is an indexer allocating alone to newly signalled deployments; a step down is another indexer joining, signal leaving, or the deployment being denied.
